purpose: LONG_DESIGN.md section 2: before the long's build, (1) does Pavo honour a 16:9 request, and (2) do two submissions in a row run at the same time (submit and leave) or one after the other?
how: Direct calls through the heroverse-pavo MCP tools from a Claude session (no GitHub Actions run, no dispatch): pavo_quote_video first (16:9, 6 s, text only: required_credits 0.0, zero_cost_confirmed true, is_estimate false), then two pavo_generate_video calls back to back, each at its own fresh exact zero-credit quote, both answered 'submitted' (no uncertain submission, nothing retried), then pavo_job polls. Clips downloaded from the Pavo CDN into the session scratchpad only (not committed) and probed with ffprobe.

submissions.name: A
submissions.prompt: the draft's s-c1-light: clouds part over a dark sea, sunbeams on the water (no people)

submissions.name: B
submissions.prompt: the draft's s-c2-river: a river parting into four streams, aerial (no people)

A.audio: aac (Pavo adds a track even with sound false: strip it, PROMPT_GUIDE)
A.frame_at_3s: full 16:9 frame, no letterbox: sunbeams through dark clouds onto the sea, as prompted

B.frame_at_3s: full 16:9 frame: a braided misty river from the air, as prompted; but small modern houses and a road at the right edge: it would fail Claude's vetting (no modern objects); the prompt needs a stated period setting

findings.aspect_16_9: YES: a 16:9 request returns 1280x720 at 24 fps (the 9:16 clips are 720x1280), the full frame used, at an exact 0-credit quote. 6 s asked, 6.58 s delivered.
findings.concurrency: YES, at least two at once: both clips were done within 6 min 58 s of the first submission, while one after the other they would need about 9.6 min at the measured 288 s a scene generation (episode.yml, 2026-10-26); and B, submitted 11 s after A, finished first, so Pavo does not run them strictly in order. One test of two clips: the limit on simultaneous jobs is not measured yet (the next test: 4 at once).
findings.for_the_design: Submit and leave works: a long's clips can be submitted chapter by chapter and collected later, the runner waiting for none of them. Each clip still needs Claude's frame check (B shows why).
